title: Execution-path telemetry playbook for prefill/decode kernel routing and attention optimizations
creator: Olivia Park
description: Create a focused playbook and implementation plan to capture per-request execution-path telemetry across the prefill and decode phases. Goal: produce coherent NVTX ranges, lightweight trace spans, and per-kernel metrics that (a) enable correlation between scheduler decisions and downstream kernel runtime characteristics, (b) make attention-path heuristics diagnosable, and (c) are low-overhead in production workloads. The playbook covers signal design, sampling policy, span naming conventions, kernel attribution tags, and an incremental rollout plan with dashboarding and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Instrumentation yields <3% median p95 added latency on representative 2k token workloads when sampling 10% of requests.
A2: NVTX/trace spans consistently encode execution-path metadata: request_id, routing_decision, kernel_variant, attention_strategy, batch_size, device_affinity.
A3: Dashboards in Grafana show per-kernel latency distribution and a heatmap correlating attention path variants with prefill/decode latencies.
A4: Playbook includes a canary rollout with toggle gates and a rollback plan; documented in Confluence.
A5: PRs with tracing changes include unit tests for span lifecycles and a microbenchmark showing CPU overhead.
A6: Implementation passes an internal perf runbook review and QA sign-off before enabling sampling >10%.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Olivia Park: Created ticket to unify tracing signals for prefill/decode. Initial spike showed noisy instrumentation when we annotated every kernel call. Proposal: move to request-scoped sparse sampling with enriched spans for sampled requests.

2026-03-11 - Samir Gupta: Spike results attached (perf microbench). Observed ~0.7% median added latency and 2.6% p95 when sampling 5% and emitting NVTX ranges + lightweight tags. Need to validate on longer sequences and mixed-batch scenarios. Proposed sampling config: time-based reservoir + deterministic hashing on request_id for reproducibility.

2026-03-12 - Marco Chen (review): Reviewed span naming table. Suggestion: avoid long freeform names in NVTX; use short canonical keys and map to human-friendly labels in Grafana via a lookup. Also recommended adding kernel_fingerprint to help group JIT/quantized kernel variants.

2026-03-12 - Design Review (Olivia Park): Decided on three-level span model: Request > Phase (prefill/decode) > Kernel. Phase spans will carry routing_decision and attention_strategy tags; kernel spans will carry kernel_variant,kernel_fingerprint,device_id,queue_wait_ms.

2026-03-13 - QA (Dana Ruiz): Will run regression harness across model-suite (gpt-family, llama-family) and dedicated pools. Test plan: 3 runs x 1M tokens, sample 1% and 10% and compare tail latency and throughput. QA to attach results by 2026-03-20.

2026-03-13 - Samir Gupta: Working on PR that implements span lifecycle helpers and a sampling abstraction (RFC in description). Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11984. Will add unit tests and microbench numbers inline. Next: add Grafana panels and a lightweight collector that forwards spans to tracing pipeline with minimal copying.
